content:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we still need to pick an approach for the console mux cutover. Two open options: 1) polymorphic shim that understands old prefilter + new router, or 2) dual-run proxy with sidecar translation. Thoughts?
aj: Leaning to polymorphic shim. Simpler runtime semantics and fewer moving parts for canarying. But we need to be explicit about RBAC checks and caching boundaries.
sam: Agreed on shim for simplicity, but warning: the shim will have to validate tokens for both legacy token shapes and new capability tokens. That affects auth latency.
li: What's the expected auth overhead? if shim does both, we might add ~2-6ms p50 but p99 could spike if external introspection is used.
frank: We can avoid external introspection by shipping a small validator lib inside the shim that reads signed capability tokens and uses local keys (rotated via KMS). Fallback to introspect only on key mismatch.
maya: That aligns with the security team preference — local validation first. For RBAC semantics: do we enforce the stricter of legacy and new, or translate legacy -> new policy?
aj: We already discussed translation mapping in the RFC appendix: map legacy roles -> capability set, then enforce new capability predicates. Translation is deterministic. If a mapping is missing, fail closed.
sam: Fail closed is safe but will block some tenants during cutover. Need a rollback plan.
li: Rollback options: feature-flag the shim at ingress layer. Also maintain a sidecar proxy plan that you can flip to if shim causes regressions.
frank: Operationally we should have a canary that routes 0.5% of traffic to shim with shadow auth enabled for 24h, collecting success/fail and latency. Shadow auth returns logged decision but does not block.
ops-bot: deploy-canary maya/shim:v1 -> 0.5% traffic routed to eng-platform-prod/shim-canary
maya: Good. Metrics to collect during canary: per-route auth latency (ms), auth failure rate, cache hit ratio (prefilter cache), p50/p95/p99 request latency, token-validation fallback count, and token-key-rotation rejections. Also collect cost delta attributable to extra CPU cycles.
aj: Add one more: route-stall occurrences where the shim waits on legacy DB for mapping. We should have a circuit-breaker of 200ms for mapping lookups.
sam: Implementation note: prefer local LRU cache for mapping, keyed by tenant-id and legacy-role-hash. TTL 10m, size cap per instance. Use consistent hashing for sticky sessions when caching matters.
li: For tenant-aware caching, we need eviction priority: high QPS tenants should have prioritized entries, low QPS tenants are fine to cold-start. That avoids thrashing.
frank: Agreed. Also implement a warmup path for dedicated tenants: prepopulate mapping on deploy via async job. Command to run locally:
```
# warmup mapping for tenant
tools/console-mux warmup --tenant tenant-123 --env prod
```
maya: Can we create a short runbook for SRE to flip canary and abort? Draft steps: 1) enable canary flag -> 0.5%; 2) monitor dashboard (auth-latency, failures) for 30m; 3) increment to 5% -> monitor 2h; 4) 25% -> monitor 6h; 5) 100% -> cutover complete. Abort if auth-failure > .1% or p99 latency increases > 40% vs baseline.
aj: Sounds good. Also require a fallback route that bypasses shim and maps to legacy proxy in case of catastrophic failure. Keep DNS TTL low for rapid re-route.
sam: Testing checklist before canary: unit tests for mapping logic, integration test against feature-flagbed legacy DB returning a few edge cases, load test for p99 auth latency at 10k rps, and a chaos test that rotates keys mid-run.
li: Who owns the mapping and translation tables? Product asked platform to provide versioned mappings with schema. We need a migration plan if mapping shape changes.
maya: Ownership stays with platform, but product signs off on mapping content. For schema changes, use versioned mapping namespace and shim reads version header in the request (or falls back to v1). Migration guideline: support both v1 and v2 for 2 weeks before removing v1.
frank: Ops note: logs must include mapping_version, token_shape, validation_path, and whether fallback introspection was used. Make sure PII is not logged.
ops-bot: create-incident-channel #shim-cutover-ops
maya: Final decision for now: build polymorphic shim with local validation + mapping translation, shadow auth for 24h canary, circuit-breaker for mapping lookups, tenant-aware cache with warmup tooling, and runbook thresholds as above. I'll file a follow-up doc with the cutover checklist and link to the PR. Anything else?
aj: Add a quick note to the console dashboard team: this will change per-route latency shape. Coordinate a dashboard panel update so alerts don't flood.
sam: I'll own the PR and run the load tests. Planning to send PR by EOW.
li: I'll prepare the SRE runbook and dashboards.
frank: I'll add the local validator lib and key-rotation handling.
maya: Great. If no objections, I'll mark RFC follow-up as accepted and schedule the canary next Tuesday. :thumbsup:
